verdict: Disney's businesses improved — segment profit rose 17% to $3.8B and entertainment streaming turned its first profit — but a $2.1B goodwill impairment on Star India and its TV networks swung the reported result to a small loss for shareholders.

segments.name: Services
segments.note: Streaming subscriptions, TV networks and channels, park tickets and hotel stays — the large majority of Disney's money.

segments.name: Products
segments.note: Merchandise, food and drinks, and other things Disney physically sells.

segmentNote: Segment operating income: Entertainment $781M, Sports $778M, Experiences $2,286M (before corporate costs).

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Marketing the movies, shows and parks, and running the company.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: The wear and tear on parks, cruise ships and equipment, spread over their working lives.

opex.name: Restructuring & impairment charges
opex.note: Writing down assets that lost value — goodwill at Star India and the entertainment linear TV networks (detailed below).

otherDetail: Interest expense, net, of $311M on Disney's debt, partly offset by $141M of equity income from companies Disney part-owns; other income was nil this quarter.
follow100Note: Of the $0.98 kept as profit per $100 of revenue, $1.07 belongs to noncontrolling partners — Disney shareholders' share was a $0.09 loss after the impairment charges. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Of the $216M of net income, $236M belongs to noncontrolling interests, leaving a $20M loss attributable to Disney (the -$0.01 EPS figure). The earnings release reports one combined cost line; the split between cost of services/products, SG&A and depreciation comes from the Q2 FY24 10-Q.

takeaways.title: Segment profit jumped
takeaways.text: Total segment operating income rose 17% to $3,845M: Experiences grew 12% to $2,286M, Entertainment jumped 72% to $781M, and Sports eased 2% to $778M on the timing of College Football Playoff games.

takeaways.title: Entertainment streaming turned profitable
takeaways.text: Disney's Entertainment direct-to-consumer business (Disney+ and Hulu) made its first quarterly profit, and Disney+ Core added more than 6 million subscribers. Disney still expected the combined streaming businesses to be profitable by Q4 of fiscal 2024.

takeaways.title: Impairments masked the progress
takeaways.text: Goodwill impairments of $2,052M — mainly Star India, which Disney agreed to contribute to a new joint venture with Reliance, plus its entertainment linear networks — swung the reported result to a $0.01-per-share loss, versus $1.21 excluding certain items.

oneTimers: Goodwill impairments of $2,052M — mainly Star India, written down as Disney agreed to contribute it to a new joint venture with Reliance, plus the entertainment linear TV networks. The charges are largely not tax deductible, which is why the tax bill stayed high relative to profit.
